discovery_focus_explanation_p1: The ballot is formed automatically to preserve diversity. It selects the most-subscribed idea from each label — ensuring each label can appear only once on the ballot, maximum 7 slots. When ideas are tied in subscriptions, the one whose labels attract more overall community engagement wins. This ensures the final vote represents the community's full range of interests, not just the most popular idea.
discovery_focus_explanation_p2:
Don't see your favorite idea?
  • Rally subscriptions to help your favorite overtake the current leader.
  • Remix a leader to improve it.
  • Propose a completely new approach.
discovery_focus_explanation_p3: The ballot updates automatically as subscriptions change. During Ballot Preparation, adjust your subscriptions to only those you want on the ballot to ensure diverse collective support. After this, the ballot freezes for the final vote.

consent_page_title: Scalable Democratic Co-Creation: Qualitative User Study
consent_study_title: Scalable Democratic Co-Creation: Qualitative User Study
consent_preamble: We would like to ask you if you are willing to participate in our software user study. Your participation is voluntary. Please read the text below carefully.
consent_section_what_investigated_a: We are designing a new digital platform to help groups make decisions collaboratively. Instead of just voting, this platform allows users to submit text proposals and edit or “remix” other people’s ideas to create new ones. We want to see how you naturally use the platform, how you decide which ideas are high quality, and how we can improve the software’s design.
consent_section_what_investigated_b: We are evaluating how users interact with the platform during a live observational session and a separate follow-up interview. We want to identify usability hurdles, understand how users rank/select proposals, and improve the design.
consent_section_who_can_participate: You can participate if you are 18 years of age or older and fluent in English or German.
consent_section_what_to_do_a: In this Method A group deployment, you will use our prototype platform over a defined period and fill out a feedback survey afterwards.
consent_section_what_to_do_b: In Method B, you will complete a synchronous observational session (screen sharing + think-aloud while using the platform). Afterwards, a separate semi-structured interview is conducted.
consent_section_rights_risks_a: Participation is voluntary. You can stop your participation at any time without any disadvantage, including by closing the browser or by not completing the survey. If you later take part in a Method B session, you can also stop the interview and stop the recording at any time. We are not aware of any physical or psychological risks.
consent_section_rights_risks_b: Participation is voluntary. You can stop the interview, stop the recording, or close the browser at any time without consequence. You can also skip any question you do not want to answer. There are no physical or psychological risks beyond normal computer use.
consent_section_compensation_a: Participation is strictly voluntary and not compensated.
consent_section_compensation_b: Participation is strictly voluntary and uncompensated.
consent_section_data_collection_a: For Method A, we collect your text proposals, platform clicks/routing behavior, arbitrarily chosen username, and survey feedback. We do not collect sensitive personal data. All data is securely stored, pseudonymized, and anonymised before any publication.
consent_section_data_collection_b: For Method B, we collect platform interaction logs, chosen username, interview responses, and (with your permission) a screen recording of the platform session. We do not collect sensitive personal data. All data is securely stored, pseudonymized, and anonymised before publication.
consent_section_funding_review: Funded by the Chair of Computational Social Science, ETH Zurich. Reviewed by the ETH Zurich Ethics Committee (Application 26 ETHICS-129).

consent_final_checkbox_a: Yes, I have read the information and consent to participate in Method A.
consent_final_checkbox_b: Yes, I have read the information and consent to participate in Method B.

consent_method_a_desc: Group Deployments & Surveys (Asynchronous). Organizational groups will be given access to the platform to collaboratively address a prompt over a set period (e.g., 1-14 days, depending on the problem complexity and group’s size). Following the deployment, participants will complete a digital survey containing the System Usability Scale (SUS) and open-ended qualitative questions regarding their experience.
consent_method_b_desc: Observational Sessions & Interviews (Synchronous). Researchers will conduct individual or small-group “shoulder viewing” sessions (in-person or via online meeting tools). Users will be asked to “think aloud” while navigating the platform. Screen recordings will be captured to document usability hurdles. This is immediately followed by a semi-structured interview.

how_it_works_process_discussion: Discuss, propose, and remix ideas. Subscribe to the ones you find interesting. (Advances after a fixed time period.)

how_it_works_concept_remix_desc: Create a new version of one or more ideas. The unified action for improving and combining.
how_it_works_concept_remix_extended: When you remix, you create a brand new idea that links back to its parent(s). The original is never changed. Remix one idea to improve it, or remix multiple ideas to combine perspectives.
how_it_works_concept_support_desc: Subscribe to ideas you find interesting. The most subscribed ideas form the Ballot.
how_it_works_concept_support_extended: Subscribe to track ideas you care about. You can subscribe to many ideas at once. As remixes appear, consider subscribing to improved versions too. The most-subscribed idea per label enters the Ballot.
how_it_works_concept_theme_desc: Labels represent different schools of thought. Each root idea creates a label. Remixes inherit their parent's labels.
how_it_works_concept_theme_extended: When you post a new idea, you create a label for it — a named tag representing your approach. Remixing an idea inherits its labels. Remixing from multiple ideas combines their labels, and you can optionally name a new label for the synthesis.
how_it_works_concept_feed_desc: Find and compare the best ideas.
how_it_works_concept_feed_extended: The Discover Feed shows you a personalized stream of Ideas. It highlights the most subscribed Ideas for each Label, allowing you to easily compare different approaches to the problem.
how_it_works_concept_ballot_desc: The community's collective focus — the most-subscribed idea per label, each label appearing only once, up to 7 slots.
how_it_works_concept_ballot_extended: The Ballot automatically assembles the most-subscribed idea from each label. Each label can appear only once on the ballot, ensuring diverse perspectives. When ideas are tied, the one whose topics attract more overall engagement wins. During the Final Vote, you rank these ideas.
how_it_works_tip_1: Post raw thoughts — they don't have to be perfect.
how_it_works_tip_2: Remix an existing idea to improve it.
how_it_works_tip_3: Subscribe to remixes you prefer over the original.
how_it_works_tip_4: Remix multiple ideas to combine perspectives.
how_it_works_tip_5: The ballot forms automatically from your subscriptions.
post_study_survey_reminder: Note: You can only fill this survey out once. Please only submit it once you are finished with the study.
how_it_works_process_coordination: Process: Collective coordination according to the rules of the system
how_it_works_process_output: Output: A single democratically selected solution to the posed problem.
how_it_works_process_discussion_detailed: During this phase, the community explores solutions. Users propose ideas, remix existing ones, and subscribe to what interests them. The most-subscribed idea per label forms the live Ballot. The phase runs for a fixed period set by the question creator.
how_it_works_process_closing_detailed: No new ideas can be created. Remix is disabled. Users can adjust their subscriptions to finalize which ideas make the ballot. This is the last chance to ensure the ballot represents the community's best ideas.
how_it_works_process_voting_detailed: The platform freezes all proposals and presents a final ballot of the leading ideas from each label. Participants rank these final options in order of their preference.
how_it_works_process_decided_detailed: The votes are tallied and a final, democratically selected solution is declared. The process is complete.
how_it_works_goal_text: The goal of this platform is to solve complex problems through structured, collective coordination. It takes a problem description as input, guides the community through an open ideation and refinement process according to the rules of the system, and produces a single, democratically selected solution as the output.
tutorial_answer_search_general: The community shares the work of sifting, creating, improving and combining ideas to create a ballot of the best ideas that are ready to vote on.
tutorial_step_problem_desc: Start by reading the full problem description in the Question tab.
tutorial_step_themes_desc: Each label represents a distinct approach to the problem. By proposing, editing, and combining, participants organically sort and refine ideas together and even combine or create new labels. Labels grow naturally through community interaction—not central algorithms.
tutorial_step_focus_desc: While you are welcome to explore everything, you are not expected to read every single idea. The 'Personal Focus' filter sorts the list based on your interactions so you can specialize in specific niches. By doing so, you share the work of sifting and improving ideas with the rest of the community—ensuring all solutions are found and refined.
tutorial_step_ballot_desc: The most leading (most supported) ideas of the top 10 labels will rise to the final Ballot.
how_this_phase_works_step1_desc: Read the background and constraints of the problem we are trying to solve.
how_this_phase_works_step2_desc: Explore the Discover feed to see what others are proposing. You can propose your own ideas or remix existing ones.
how_this_phase_works_step3_desc: Add labels to ideas to organize them into distinct categories or themes. This helps the community group similar concepts.
how_this_phase_works_step4_desc: Subscribe to the ideas you support. The most subscribed ideas from each label will make it to the final ballot.
how_this_phase_works_step5_desc: The ballot is a summary of all subscribed ideas during this phase. In the next phase, no new ideas can be added, only subscriptions can be distributed or removed.

This ballot was formed automatically to preserve diversity: each label can appear only once, and the most-subscribed idea represents each label. Ties are broken by overall topic engagement. final_result_borda_explanation: This vote used Borda count scoring. With {n} proposals, voters ranked them from their favourite to least favourite. Being ranked 1st earns the most points, and each lower rank earns one fewer point. Proposals with higher scores had stronger overall support across all voters.

consent_section_data_processing: All collected data is processed and stored securely on ETH Zurich servers.
consent_section_anonymization: Any personal identifiers, such as arbitrarily chosen usernames, are strictly anonymized and replaced with randomized IDs in the final dataset before publication.
consent_section_secondary_use: The fully anonymized research data (such as text proposals and system logs) may be shared indefinitely in open-access repositories for secondary use by other researchers.
consent_section_retention: Personal data, such as email addresses provided for receiving study results, are stored separately from the research data and will be deleted after six months. The anonymized research data is retained indefinitely for scientific sharing.
